In the mighty name of Jesus, I offer immense gratitude to Jesus and the Blessed Mother for raising me up as a living witness to Her apparition. I begin my testimony.
My name is Sheena George. Today, my name is Dr. Sheena George, and this title of 'Doctor' is a precious gift bestowed upon me by our Blessed Mother.
No matter how much I thank Her, it will never be enough, and it is to express this gratitude through my testimony that the Mother has blessed me to stand at this Holy Altar.
I entered into my Covenant on 8/11/2024, and I come from Pala.
Speaking of the Covenant, I am someone who entered into this without ever expecting to do so.
Furthermore, regarding my PhD, it had been ten long years of struggle, and this past March 25th was the Feast of the Annunciation of our Blessed Mother.
That was the exact day of my open defense, the day the Blessed Mother miraculously awarded me my doctorate.
I pursued my PhD in Commerce, and my topic was 'The Influence of Retail Therapy on Consumers' Mood Variation: A Kerala Perspective'.
It was a Kerala perspective study, but it is actually the very first study of its kind from an Indian perspective.
Usually, five years is the standard term for completing a PhD, and within that term, I had completed a draft of my thesis.
But my guide was completely uncooperative, and I am choosing not to mention the name of the university to maintain anonymity.
My guide would constantly harass me and completely refused to review my work.
I was heartbroken and suffered immensely, and after those five years had passed, I had to apply for an extension again.
When I submitted multiple applications for the extension, the staff in that university section were completely unhelpful.
The head of the department was also extremely harassing, refusing to offer any assistance to move the process forward.
I went through terrible hardships, enduring severe mental stress, torment, and agony over this.
Enduring all this suffering, after the initial five years, I spent another three agonizing years struggling for extensions.
By the eighth year, the university abruptly closed my file.
They told me I would never be able to get my PhD, claiming my guide had not submitted the proper documents.
I would often approach my guide and plead, but he would give me documents with falsified details and altered dates.
The university refused to accept any of these manipulated documents, completely disregarding my hard work.
Even though I had completed national and international presentations and publications, the university rejected everything.
In my eighth year, they explicitly told me to leave, demanding that I exit the campus and never return.
They chased me away, and on that day, honestly, I thought my story was entirely over. Crying bitterly,
I walked out of that university and stood there completely lost, before finally returning home.
Back at home, as the days passed from November 5th, 2024, my situation worsened.
I lost sleep and fell into a deep depression, completely overwhelmed with sorrow and unable to do anything.
I felt entirely abnormal, and then, at 5:00 AM, I clearly heard a voice saying, "Sheena, I am going to Kreupasanam."
I heard that voice twice, and I wasn't fully asleep; I was just lying there in bed.
I jumped up and looked everywhere around the room, feeling completely startled and confused.
Then I thought it sounded like the voice of a friend who studied tenth grade with me, so I checked if she had messaged me on WhatsApp.
I wondered what it was, but there were no messages, and that Saturday simply passed by in confusion.
On Sunday, I called her to ask... but truthfully, falling at the feet of our Blessed Mother, I humbly beg for forgiveness now.
I had never thought highly of Kreupasanam; my mind was entirely consumed by extreme logical thinking.
All my thoughts were driven by secular logic, making it impossible for me to blindly believe in such miracles.
I had committed the grave sin of criticizing such spiritual matters and intercessions in the past.
After hearing that mysterious voice, when I called my friend on Sunday, she told me she hadn't said anything.
However, she then prophetically added, "It is time for you to go there, my dear."
I then asked my husband, who is a very good man, but he was slightly confused about whether we should really go pray at Kreupasanam in Alappuzha.
When I pleaded with him to take me, he hesitated and suggested alternative plans. As we are from Pala,
He said, "We have the Blessed Mother's Novena there, so why don't you just go there?"
He told me he was too busy to accompany me, but miraculously, at 10:30 that night,
He came to me and asked, "When do you want to go to Kreupasanam?", and that is how I ended up taking the Covenant.
Honestly, I didn't even know what taking the Covenant fully meant; I sat and listened to the entire preparation class.
I only understood half of it, and the deeper spiritual meaning of the Covenant completely went over my head.
Yet, it felt as though someone was leading me blindfolded, guiding me to take that sacred Covenant.
After taking the Covenant, I returned home, and that very evening, the Blessed Mother inspired my heart.
I lit the green candle and made a firm resolution as I spoke directly to Mother Mary, knowing I could never go back on my word.
With the green candle lit during my evening prayers, I dedicated myself entirely to the Covenant.
I tried my best to understand its depth and strictly observed it, because it was a sacred promise made to the Blessed Mother. And I continued moving forward.
As days went by, I kept visiting the university, desperately hoping to move things forward in some way.
It was then, in the first week of February, that I heard a voice and saw Father Joseph on a TV screen.
Father prophesied, saying, "By the 25th, everything will be set right."
He repeated it twice, waving a silver-colored staff...
I wondered which 25th he meant; February 25th came and went, but nothing happened.
So, I decided to go back to the university on March 25th, and every time I went to see my guide, I would secretly intercede.
Without anyone noticing, I would silently intercede and sprinkle blessed salt on the section officer's table, my guide's table, and along the university corridors.
As I sprinkled the salt, I would earnestly pray, "Mother, come with me, Mother, please walk ahead of me."
From then on, I always walked holding tightly onto the hem of our Blessed Mother's mantle. When I went there in the first week of March, absolutely nothing had changed.
I saw a lady sitting in the Deputy Registrar's chair, and I went up to her and broke down in tears.
I sobbed and said, "Madam, everything is over for me; please, can you help me?"
She made some calls to the office, but then coldly told me that nothing could be done and asked me to leave.
However, the 25th was approaching, though I wasn't hyper-aware of the date's significance at the time.
I reassured myself, knowing this was a matter entirely taken over by our Blessed Mother; I decided not to step back, trusting that Mother would lead and I would follow.
That was my only conviction, and I told them I would return on the 25th, which was when my husband and I traveled outside Kerala.
When we arrived and walked in, I saw that the previously arrogant section officer was sitting with his head bowed.
This was the same man who used to chase everyone away, the one who would furiously kick me out the moment he saw me.
The very man who told me never to return was sitting submissively, and he suddenly called someone over.
He instructed them, saying, "Take her to the Deputy Registrar's office," and when I went there, a miraculous sight awaited me.
I saw the Deputy Registrar in the same office where I had seen that lady before, but it was not the old registrar.
There was a complete divine transformation; her face was entirely glowing with a heavenly grace, and she was wearing a solid blue saree without a single print.
Dressed entirely in blue—she gently asked me, "What do you need?"
When I began explaining my situation, she compassionately said, "Okay, sit here."
As I briefly explained, she acted as if she already knew everything through divine intercession, not making me speak much, and immediately called the staff.
She summoned the staff from the research section and sternly questioned them, asking for the exact reason.
She demanded to know why they hadn't accepted my documents and why my submission was denied.
When they mumbled some lame excuses, she turned to me and asked what documents I had, and I handed over everything.
I gave her all my files, complete with abstracts, research papers, and all the original documents.
By then, they verified everything, asked what was missing in it, and told me to take the entire thing and file it.
The order was issued, and then they said, "Her guide is very problematic, the guide won't help."
Then suddenly, she stood up, took out her personal mobile, and started calling the guide, but the people in the office said,
"Madam, we don't have the provision to call like that, the university cannot call and instruct the guide."
She didn't listen to any of it, and saying, "I will call," she took the phone.
She called him and said, "Within three days, you must conduct her pre-presentation and pre-submission viva voce, and the report must reach here."
After saying that, she didn't speak another word to me, just made a hand gesture like this.
She told me to go to the guide, and so, when I went to the guide, he was frantic, getting the external examiner and everyone ready.
He was rushing to conduct the pre-submission viva voce there.
Thus, on the fourth day, the viva voce took place.
After that, on the fifth day, when I went to submit all the reports to the university,
the sight I saw and came to know was that the section head was not sitting there; he had been suspended.
To tell you the truth, I was in disbelief, but did Mother Mary show me that much immense mercy?
Next, even before that in December, an order had come stating that all guides must behave respectfully with the scholars.
How did all this happen, why did it happen, and for whom did it come? I only know that it came for me.
Thus, the procedures for my submission were moving forward, but the guide was still quite angry.
He said, "I don't know if your submission will happen or not," but after saying that,
I proceeded again in March...April for various things, but in 20th April,
when I went near my guide at the research center, the sight I saw was my thesis opened on a laptop.
He had it opened, and because until then he was someone who hadn't even opened and read it properly,
he was doing some formatting and other things with the help of someone who knew the technical side.
That was the scene I saw, and thus, by the 22nd,
he sent me a PDF copy and told me, "Check this for plagiarism and take it."
So, that same evening, I checked for plagiarism, and there was only a very small percentage of plagiarism.
That too is solely the grace and blessing of Mother Mary in every single matter, and it was only because of that, that my thesis was ready.
I was getting it ready for submission, and its typesetting and binding had to be done.
From the print house on the 23rd, my guide called me and asked me to come there.
When I rushed there, the sight I saw was the guide standing there, having signed all eight copies of the thesis given for binding.
He is standing there, and I wondered if I should believe my eyes; without Mother Mary giving this grace, how could this happen?
He was standing there and told me, "Put your signatures and take them with you, but I am not sure if your submission will take place."
So the next day, on the 24th, with this thesis and documents,
I went to the university in the morning, and when there were some delays and obstacles there too,
I kept praying to Mother Mary, and many people were also interceding for me to Mother Mary.
Those who come to Kreupasanam and know the Blessed Mother, and also the blessed salt...
I sprinkled that blessed salt there to remove all obstacles, calling upon Mother Mary, praying, "Mother, please stand before me."
I went around there praying continuously, and thus, by 5:30 PM, my submission was successfully completed.
After it happened, usually, there are three evaluations at the university, one of which is a foreign university evaluation.
Everyone has anxiety about this, and the previous ones done by my guide had required resubmissions, so I too had anxiety.
Even so, because Mother Mary was with me, somehow, my anxiety would come, and just as it came, it would fly away.
I didn't have any other worries, but normally, it takes more than a year for the evaluation to be completed and returned there.
Even though I submitted it on March 25th, in the first week of this past February 2026, my guide called me.
He said, "All your thesis evaluations have been completed and returned, let's conduct the open defense at the end of February."
I was absolutely astounded, and then I was reading these reports, and when I read them, the sight I saw, truly,
I am testifying, it is not my thesis! Because, regarding that thesis,
it had gone abroad to Birmingham University in London, and my guide asked me, "Whom did you catch hold of to send it there?"
He asked, "Who advocated for you at the university?"
When all these things happened like this, and then, the professor who conducted the evaluation at Birmingham University said—it was an appreciation note.
It was really written like a report: "In the Indian perspective, this is a new study, and in Western universities, this should be recommended."
Similarly, in this thesis, from all three evaluators, there was not even a single correction; Mother Mary is the one who looked after that thesis.
It was Mother who wrote the thesis, otherwise, how could I achieve it; the thesis came back without a single correction like that.
Likewise, the professor from Rajkot University and others spoke about the thesis with such appreciation, and this is the first part of my testimony.
Then, I saw Mother, Mother Mary, directly.
One day, I told Mother Mary, after the first renewal of my Covenant, I told Mother, "Mother, I desire to see you, but perhaps I am not worthy of it.
Mother, if I could just see you, I would be so happy," that's all I said.
Then, that evening, the sight I saw... my own mother is not in my hometown right now, but my mother came to the head of the bed where I was lying.
She came and said, "I came to see you then again she said, I came up again just to see you, I stepped in here just for that."
I thought, "My mummy isn't here, right?" and suddenly, as I was sitting there, a blue light came onto my face.
From amidst twinkling stars, this Mother, the Mother of Kreupasanam, came before me.
She looked at me and smiled, and then I saw Mother again; Mother came near me and gave me a Holy Rosary.
I sat up and prayed that entire Rosary, and in the same way, at different times, people named Mary came.
Similarly, when I first started distributing the Kreupasanam newsletters, I would come every possible month.
I usually buy four bundles, five bundles, or now six bundles of the paper, and so when that happened, the fact that my very first paper was bought by Mother Mary became clear to me.
When I took the Covenant at Kreupasanam, I had a huge status issue. I am working as a college Assistant Professor,
so at that time, I was on a career break. During that time, I thought, since I am on leave, I took the papers to distribute, deciding to go to Kreupasanam.
I thought I would go to make a good Confession next week, but as I was going, I felt very hesitant to distribute these papers.
The students from the college where I teach in Pala, and their parents, might see me.
If they did, while I was distributing the paper, I thought they would wonder what this teacher is doing.
But even so, I told Mother Mary, "Mother, I don't want these worthless thoughts, am I not your daughter?"
"From now on, I will distribute the paper; I must distribute the paper everywhere, and I must tell everyone."
"I must tell my students and everyone about Mother." Saying this, as I went, I suddenly got into a bus, which was a blue bus.
On the back of the blue bus, behind the driver's seat, there was a large picture of Mother Mary.
I went and sat next to an older lady, and that lady was sitting there, not really paying attention.
So I asked... after a little while, when we came near a church, she made the Sign of the Cross, so I thought, she probably won't scold me.
"Sister, sister, may I give you a Kreupasanam paper?" I asked.
Then she suddenly turned, and on that face, that face and those eyes had an immense, heavenly power.
Then they asked me, "Daughter, wasn't it when you had no other way out that you went to Kreupasanam and took the Covenant?",
I replied, "Yes, but now I have strong faith," and I laughed, but I didn't tell anyone that I was going to Confession.
I had absolutely no awareness that one or two things related to my character, which involved certain dealings, I did were sins.
When I remembered those things, I laughed, because I truly didn't know they were sins.
That woman explained everything to me with examples, and I don't know why she told me all that.
I couldn't even get up and leave her side, and finally, when the bus stopped, it was with great difficulty that I got off.
So, when I went to Confession after getting off, I had a few more sins to confess! I was able to confess them all,
and I confessed them, and now I know for sure that Mother Mary is with me every single day.
Every day, she doesn't just follow me, but she goes before me, holding my hand.
There is nothing left for my Mother to do for me, nothing left for her to provide in my life, and nothing will happen that Mother doesn't desire.
Nothing will happen without her will, and I am standing in this holy presence praying for my generations, so that my children and your generations may be blessed.
I pray that we all live looking towards eternity, and that my family and I are sustained as witnesses to Mother's apparition.
This is my only prayer to sustain all of us.
Because I know that when I receive that wisdom, the wisdom of the Holy Spirit, Mother will surely grant me all blessings and graces.
Through Mother's intercession, Jesus will grant them to me, for I also have a very close and loving relationship with Jesus.
During my college days, I was deeply in love with Jesus.
But after that, I became a bit detached, and as my logical thinking increased, I forgot all that and walked away from Jesus.
I forgot all that and walked away from Jesus, but that deep internal hook remained right here in my heart.
Later on, especially after I took this Covenant, I began to deeply feel the presence of Baby Jesus.
I started experiencing Baby Jesus calling me and walking around me, and sometimes He would come and tap my feet.
Sometimes, when I am lying down, it feels like a small, colorful wooden toy gently tapping on my head and leaving.
I have had so many incredibly sweet and cute experiences like that.
I absolutely love to talk and hear about Baby Jesus, and all those experiences are still with me.
We have been living in a rented house for many years, as we have been staying in rentals for almost 20 years due to our jobs.
At that time, I spoke to Mother Mary about the rented house we were living in.
We couldn't move out of there, and it was in a terrible condition, filled with dust, causing me severe allergic sicknesses.
I said to Mother, "Mother, I have a deep desire to live in a good house, could you quickly bless me with a nice rented house?"
I asked her to quickly give us a house, and then, one day, I had a vision of Mother walking around the rented house we were living in.
I saw her walking around sprinkling salt, and soon after that, my husband suddenly came to me.
He said, "Let's buy that plot of land right next door," and now we already have a plan ready for our house.
I told Mother, "Mother, you must give me a house that you design, a house that is pleasing to you," and that is my prayer for the house now.
Regarding my apostolic work, my ministry of distributing the publication, I usually get into the bus from the back door.
I board the KSRTC buses from the rear and distribute it to everyone, at auto stands and bus stands.
I intentionally try to choose places like that, where people from all backgrounds, including non-Christians, gather, to distribute the publication.
When I distribute the publication, I always make sure to keep a few blessed medals with me.
Even when some elderly mothers say, "Daughter, we can't go there," when talking about Mother Mary, I share my own testimony.
I tell them about the message in the newsletter, and then I give them the medal, and that is how I do it.
As for works of mercy, normally when I am walking through the town, I sometimes bring packed meals from home to give away.
Even though I bring meals from home, more often, when people approach us asking for help, I do something more.
God gave me the great blessing to not just give them money, but to ask them if they are hungry, and the grace to feed the hungry.
God gave me the great blessing to ask them if they are hungry, and the profound grace to feed the hungry.
I ask them what they want and what they like, and buying it for them gives me immense joy.
